
{{alias}}( sortOrder, N, D )
    Sorts a double-precision floating-point strided array in increasing or
    decreasing order using quicksort, with insertion sort for small partitions
    (size <= 20).

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use typed
    array views.

    Parameters
    ----------
    sortOrder: string
        Sort direction.

    N: integer
        Number of elements to sort.

    D: Float64Array
        Array to sort in-place.

    Returns
    -------
    out: integer
        Status code. If successful, the function returns `0`; otherwise, the
        function returns `-i`, where `i` is the index of the argument having an
        invalid value.

    Examples
    --------
    > var D = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 5, 7, 9, 3, 11 ] );
    > {{alias}}( 'increasing', 5, D );
    > D
    <Float64Array>[ 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 ]

    // Using typed array views:
    > var D0 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 99, 5, 7, 9, 3, 11 ] );
    > D = new Float64Array( D0.buffer, D0.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*1 );
    > {{alias}}( 'increasing', 5, D );
    > D0
    <Float64Array>[ 99, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray( sortOrder, N, D,strideD,offsetD, stack,strideS,offsetS )
    Sorts a double-precision floating-point strided array in increasing or
    decreasing order using quicksort, with insertion sort for small partitions
    (size <= 20) and using alternative indexing semantics.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the offset parameter supports indexing semantics based on a starting
    index.

    Parameters
    ----------
    sortOrder: string
        Sort direction.

    N: integer
        Number of elements to sort.

    D: Float64Array
        Array to sort in-place.

    strideD: integer
        Stride length for `D`.

    offsetD: integer
        Starting index for `D`.

    stack: Float64Array
        Workspace array. Must have at least `64` indexed elements.

    strideS: integer
        Stride length for `stack`.

    offsetS: integer
        Starting index for `stack`.

    Returns
    -------
    out: integer
        Status code. If successful, the function returns `0`; otherwise, the
        function returns `-i`, where `i` is the index of the argument having an
        invalid value.

    Examples
    --------
    > var D = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 5, 7, 9, 3, 11 ] );
    > var stack = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 64 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 'increasing', 5, D, 1, 0, stack, 1, 0 );
    > D
    <Float64Array>[ 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 ]

    // Using typed array views:
    > var D0 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 99, 5, 7, 9, 3, 11 ] );
    > var s0 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 65 );
    > D = new Float64Array( D0.buffer, D0.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*1 );
    > s = new Float64Array( stack0.buffer, s0.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*1 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 'increasing', 5, D, 1, 0, s, 1, 0 );
    > D0
    <Float64Array>[ 99, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 ]

    See Also
    --------
